passage: My name is Tara and I am in the same class as Mridul. At playtime a big boy grabbed Sumit's cap and held it up high. Sumit is Mridul's brother. This morning on the bus they were shouting at each other, so I thought Mridul would go away. But he walked over and stood right next to Sumit. His hands were shaking a little, but maybe he was just cold, I don't know. He said, "Give it back." Then he took Sumit's hand and they went to tell Miss. I saw them talking to her.

qa.q: What did the big boy take from Sumit?
qa.a: The big boy grabbed Sumit's cap.

qa.q: What might Mridul have been feeling as he stood beside Sumit?
qa.a: Mridul may have been scared but wanted to protect his brother. Tara notices his shaking hands but says she cannot be sure, so it is only a clue.

qa.q: What did Mridul do that was wise, and what else could he try?
qa.a: Mridul stood by Sumit and then went to tell Miss instead of fighting. If the boy keeps bothering them, they can keep telling a teacher. 👍

qa.q: How might Sumit see it when Mridul stands next to him?
qa.a: Sumit may feel safe and cared for, even though they were shouting on the bus. It shows that being brothers can matter more than an argument.

grounding: A child stands with a brother on the playground despite a morning fight at home, and they tell a teacher rather than fight, seen by a classmate.
